description: Test suite registry for scripts/run_tests.py (REQ-DEVOPS-046, ADR-000186). A suite is one runner; a group is one invocation of it. Tiers are cumulative: t1 runs t0 plus the affected unit groups, t2 adds the affected integration / GUI groups, t3 runs every suite and group whatever changed. perf, stress, soak, live and package are explicit lanes, never implied by a tier. 'project' is the qmake project that builds the binary, 'uses' the projects whose binaries the suite executes, 'inputs' the non-code files it reads (globs, repository-relative). expected_seconds are measured single-process wall times; shards split a group across processes (balanced by recorded per-case duration through PROJECT_TEST_CASES, else PROJECT_TEST_SHARD). 'load_sensitive' lists timing-sensitive functional cases: they still run and must pass, in an exclusive job after the parallel phase. 'wrapper' runs a group under another program (e.g. xvfb-run for a GUI group that needs a display; '{display}' is replaced per shard). 'cases' / 'exclude_cases' (globs) give a group part of its runner's cases, e.g. hardware cases to the live lane with requirement 'hardware'. 'requires' entries: 'file:<path>', 'exe:<name>', 'python:<module>', 'testdata' ($PROJECT_TEST_DATA), 'hardware' ($PROJECT_LIVE_HW_ARGS). PROJECT-SPECIFIC: register the project's own suites here; '_example_binary_suite' shows the shape of a binary suite and is not loaded.

t1.summary: t0 + unit groups of the affected suites

t2.summary: t1 + integration and GUI groups of the affected suites (the work-item gate)

t3.summary: every suite and group, affected or not (system / expensive tests; nightly / pre-release; run it on the Debug and the Release tree)

perf.summary: benchmarks and throughput assertions, one at a time

stress.summary: stress groups, one at a time

live.summary: live application verification scripts on real data / hardware

package.summary: staged distribution: the project's package validation + asserting smoke test

release.summary: release validation of a built package (the project's release checks); never implied by a tier
